content: 1. Nelfinavir increases the plasma concentration and effects of doravirine by inhibiting its metabolism through the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction may lead to elevated toxicity. Close monitoring is required when co-administering these drugs. 2. Nelfinavir elevates the levels and effects of doxepin cream by altering its metabolism via the CYP3A4 enzyme. Caution and close monitoring are advised during co-administration. 3. Nelfinavir enhances the plasma concentration and effects of doxorubicin by interfering with its metabolism through CYP3A4. This interaction necessitates careful monitoring and caution. 4. Nelfinavir increases the levels and effects of liposomal doxorubicin by affecting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Close monitoring is recommended to mitigate potential toxicities. 5. Nelfinavir raises the plasma concentration and effects of dronabinol by altering its metabolism via the hepatic enzyme CYP2E1. This interaction requires caution and close monitoring. Additionally, nelfinavir significantly increases dronabinol levels through CYP3A4 inhibition, necessitating the use of alternative drugs to avoid serious toxicities. 6. Dronedarone increases the levels and effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4 and by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Close monitoring is required. Conversely, nelfinavir elevates dronedarone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and alternative drugs should be considered due to the risk of severe interactions. 7. Drospirenone slightly increases nelfinavir levels by affecting its metabolism through CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown but considered minor. 8. Nelfinavir increases the plasma concentration and effects of dutasteride by altering its metabolism through CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and uncertain. 9. Nelfinavir elevates the levels and effects of duvelisib by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increases duvelisib exposure, raising the risk of toxicities. The duvelisib dose should be reduced to 15 mg twice daily, and close monitoring is required. 10. Nelfinavir increases the levels and effects of edoxaban by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Alternative drugs are recommended due to the risk of serious interactions. Dose adjustments may be necessary when using strong P-gp inhibitors. 11. Efavirenz decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Conversely, nelfinavir slightly increases efavirenz levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, but the clinical significance is minor and uncertain. 12. Nelfinavir significantly increases the levels and effects of elacestrant by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Alternative drugs should be used to avoid serious toxicities. 13. Elagolix increases nelfinavir levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Nelfinavir also increases elagolix levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Co-administration of elagolix 200 mg twice daily with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. 14. Nelfinavir significantly increases the levels and effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by inhibiting their metabolism through CYP3A4. Alternative drugs should be used to avoid serious toxicities. 15. Nelfinavir increases eletriptan levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This interaction is contraindicated, and administration should be separated by at least 72 hours. 16. Nelfinavir significantly increases eliglustat levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This interaction is contraindicated, especially in poor or intermediate metabolizers. Dose adjustments are required for extensive metabolizers. 17. Nelfinavir increases eluxadoline levels by decreasing its metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended. If co-administered with OATP1B1 inhibitors, the eluxadoline dose should be reduced to 75 mg twice daily. 18. Nelfinavir increases elvitegravir levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are required. Co-administration with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF is contraindicated. 19. Nelfinavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when co-administered with emtricitabine. Close monitoring is advised. 20. Nelfinavir increases encorafenib levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Alternative drugs are recommended. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, the encorafenib dose should be reduced to one-third of the original dose. 21. Nelfinavir increases the levels and effects of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring is required to manage potential toxicities. 22. Nelfinavir increases the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome when co-administered with enfuvirtide. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 23. Nelfinavir significantly increases entrectinib levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is not recommended. Alternative drugs should be used. 24. Enzalutamide decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing its metabolism through CYP3A4. Conversely, nelfinavir increases enzalutamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. This interaction is contraindicated. 25. Nelfinavir slightly increases eplerenone levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor and uncertain. 26. Nelfinavir significantly increases erdafitinib levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Alternative drugs are recommended. If co-administration is unavoidable, close monitoring and dose adjustments are necessary. 27. Nelfinavir significantly increases ergonovine and ergotamine levels by inhibiting their metabolism through CYP3A4. These interactions are contraindicated. 28. Nelfinavir increases erlotinib levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are required. 29. Erythromycin base increases nelfinavir levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative drugs are recommended due to the risk of serious interactions. 30. Nelfinavir increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. This interaction increases the risk of serotonin syndrome and requires close monitoring. 31. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases nelfinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism but increases nelfinavir levels via CYP2C19 inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are advised. 32. Esomeprazole decreases nelfinavir levels, potentially leading to virologic failure. This interaction is contraindicated. 33. Nelfinavir increases estradiol levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required to manage potential toxicities. 34. Nelfinavir increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. The starting dose of eszopiclone should be reduced to 1 mg/day, and close monitoring is required. 35. Nelfinavir significantly alters ethinyl estradiol levels, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 36. Nelfinavir increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Close monitoring is required to manage potential toxicities. 37. Nelfinavir increases etonogestrel levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Close monitoring is advised. 38. Nelfinavir increases etoposide levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. Caution and close monitoring are required. 39. Etravirine increases nelfinavir levels by decreasing its metabolism, while nelfinavir increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Close monitoring is required. 40. Nelfinavir slightly increases eucalyptus levels by inhibiting its metabolism through CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor.
